seoDescription: Methods, code and benchtop protocols from the Churchman Lab: GeneWalk, NET-seq, nano-COP, subcellular RNA-seq and mitoribosome profiling, with analysis scripts on GitHub and post-publication corrections.
title: Experimental and computational methods
intro: We develop methods for studying transcription, RNA processing, RNA flow between cellular compartments and mitochondrial gene expression. Published protocols, software and analysis code are available below and on GitHub; post-publication corrections are listed with the corresponding protocol.

cards.title: GeneWalk
cards.body: Works out which of a gene's annotated functions are actually relevant in your experimental context, using representation learning on a condition-specific gene network.

cards.title: Benchtop protocols
cards.body: NET-seq, nano-COP, subcellular RNA-seq and mitoribosome profiling — published protocols with PDFs and matching analysis pipelines.
cards.imageAlt: Bench work in the Churchman lab

cards.title: Code
cards.body: Analysis pipelines for every method we publish, plus GeneWalk itself, live under the churchmanlab organization on GitHub.

items.name: nano-COP — nanopore analysis of co-transcriptional processing
items.citation: Drexler HL, Choquet K, Merens HE, Tang PS, Simpson JT, Churchman LS (2021) Revealing nascent RNA processing dynamics with nano-COP. Nature Protocols 16(3):1343–1375.
items.correction: Page 18, In-house 10× poly(A) buffer (for poly(A) tailing only) should read: “Contains 25 mM MnCl₂, 10 mM DTT, and 5 mg/ml BSA. Mix 1 μl of 1 M MnCl₂, 4 μl of 100 mM DTT, 4 μl of 50 mg/ml BSA, and 31 μl of nuclease-free water.” 1 M MnCl₂ can be purchased from Sigma (cat. no. M1785).
